claims.text: High-entropy alloys exhibit temperature-dependent plastic deformation behavior.
Temperature-dependent plastic deformation in HEAs can be understood using in situ TEM with heating and deformation capabilities.
Properties of HEAs can be optimized using insights obtained through in situ heating and deformation TEM.
The proposed materials are polycrystalline HEAs with varying compositions and microstructures.
The proposed investigation applies in situ TEM with heating and deformation capabilities.
The HEAs are to be investigated at multiple temperatures and deformation rates.
Grain size mediates temperature-dependent plastic deformation in HEAs.
Grain-boundary segregation mediates temperature-dependent plastic deformation in HEAs.
Precipitate formation mediates temperature-dependent plastic deformation in HEAs.
Thermally activated dislocation motion is an underlying deformation mechanism in HEAs.
Grain-boundary-mediated deformation is an underlying deformation mechanism in HEAs.
Observing microstructural evolution and deformation mechanisms will improve understanding of temperature-dependent plastic deformation in HEAs.
Improved mechanistic understanding will enable optimization of HEA properties for specific applications.
The effects of grain size, grain-boundary segregation, and precipitate formation on HEA mechanical properties are not fully understood.
Dislocation density, grain-boundary segregation, precipitate formation, and deformation rate can be measured during the proposed experiment.
